bill.title: Keeping All Students Safe Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates schools and Head Start programs, imposing new training requirements, compliance procedures, and enforcement obligations on educational institutions.
The bill creates a new private right of action for students subjected to unlawful seclusion or restraint, which would generate litigation opportunities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit schools and Head Start programs that receive federal funding from using seclusion (confining a student alone in a locked room) and would restrict the use of physical restraints to situations where a student poses an imminent danger of serious physical injury. It requires staff training in crisis intervention, establishes procedures for reporting incidents, and creates enforcement mechanisms including the ability for students to sue and for federal agencies to withhold payments from programs that violate the rules. The bill also provides grants to help state education agencies implement these policies.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, teachers, and the families paying for it.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: EASE Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: The bill directly establishes a payment model for federally qualified health centers, rural health clinics, critical access hospitals, and rural emergency hospitals to furnish specialty care services.
The bill requires digital methods and telehealth technology to deliver remote specialty care, creating demand for broadband and telecommunications infrastructure in rural areas.
The bill's reliance on telehealth platforms and digital coordination systems would affect vendors providing health IT and telemedicine software solutions.
The bill modifies service delivery and reimbursement models for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, which may affect how insurers and managed-care organizations structure networks and payments.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a program that uses networks of rural health providers to deliver specialty medical care remotely to Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP patients in rural areas. The networks must include at least 50 qualifying rural clinics or hospitals, be nonprofit, and use telehealth technology to connect patients with specialists while coordinating with their primary care doctors. At least half of the providers in each network must be located in rural areas.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who sees a doctor or pays for care.

bill.title: A bill to provide for the transfer of administrative jurisdiction over certain Federal land in the State of California, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 486.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects cattle ranchers currently grazing on the transferred land by changing which federal agency manages their grazing permits.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would transfer management of certain federal land between Yosemite National Park and Stanislaus National Forest in California. The transfer is designed to move land currently used for cattle grazing from National Park Service control to Forest Service control, because the Forest Service's multiple-use management approach is better suited to accommodate grazing activities. The change would align land management with existing use patterns.

plain.whoItTouches: People who visit public land, and people who live beside it. People who live near or work on federal land.

districtAwards.description: APPLICATION PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS NEW TRANSIT SERVICE IS TO IMPROVE MOBILITY AND CONNECTIVITY IN THE TRANSIT-DEPENDENT PROJECT AREA. THE PROJECT WILL SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS (GHG) AND VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED IMPROVE SAFETY AND TRAFFIC CONGESTION SUPPORT THE CREATION OF JOBS AND INCREASE TRANSIT RIDERSHIP. THESE IMPROVEMENTS WILL GREATLY BENEFIT THE REGION WHICH HAS THE WORST AIR QUALITY AND TRAFFIC CONGESTION IN THE COUNTRY AND COMPRISES ABOUT HALF OF CALIFORNIAS DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITY POPULATION. SPECIFICALLY THE PROJECT AIMS TO:* IMPROVE MOBILITY IN THE EASTERN SAN FERNANDO VALLEY BY INTRODUCING AN IMPROVED NORTH-SOUTH TRANSIT CONNECTION BETWEEN KEY TRANSIT HUBS/ROUTES;* PROVIDE A NEW AND MORE RELIABLE TRANSIT OPTION THAT IMPROVES PASSENGER MOBILITY AND ENHANCES TRANSIT ACCESSIBILITY/CONNECTIVITY FOR RESIDENTS TO LOCAL AND REGIONAL DESTINATIONS AND ACTIVITY CENTERS;* INCREASE TRANSIT SERVICE EFFICIENCY (E.G. SPEEDS AND PASSENGER THROUGHPUT); AND* ENCOURAGE A MODAL SHIFT FROM DRIVING TO ACHIEVE REDUCTIONS IN GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS.; ACTIVITIES PERFORMED: THE SCOPE OF THE EAST SAN FERNANDO VALLEY LIGHT RAIL TRANSIT PROJECT COMPRISES 6.7 MILES OF 11 STATIONS 11 TRACTION POWER SUBSTATIONS OVERHEAD CONTACT SYSTEM 34 VEHICLES AND A MAINTENANCE AND STORAGE FACILITY. IT ALSO INCLUDES ROW ACQUISITION RELOCATION COMMUNICATIONS/SIGNALING BUILDINGS BIKE PARKING AND PEDESTRIAN/VEHICLE ACCESS ARE INCLUDED. THE LIGHT RAIL TRANSIT SYSTEM WILL OPERATE ALONG A SEMI-EXCLUSIVE RIGHT OF WAY IN THE MEDIAN OF VAN NUYS BOULEVARD SEPARATED BY A BARRIER EXCEPT AT SIGNALIZED INTERSECTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL CONNECT KEY DESTINATIONS AND CREATE OPPORTUNITIES TO ACCESS THE GROWING SAN FERNANDO VALLEY SUBREGION AND OTHER AREAS OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY. IT WILL ALSO IMPROVE TRAVEL BETWEEN THE SAN FERNANDO VALLEY SUBREGION AND THE WESTSIDE CITIES SUBREGION OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY AFTER THE COMPLETION ON METROS SEPULVEDA TRANSIT CORRIDOR PROJECT. MEANWHILE THE PROJECTS STATIONS LOCATED NEAR METRO LOCAL AND RAPID EAST/WEST BUS SERVICE WILL IMPROVE SYSTEM CONNECTIVITY. A DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT IS PROVIDED IN ATTACHMENT 1. ATTACHMENT 2 INCLUDES FIGURES SHOWING THE PROJECTS LOCATION IN THE CONTEXT OF THE EXISTING AND FUTURE TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM.; EXPECTED OUTCOMES: GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS REDUCTION BY 1084556 METRIC TONS REDUCE TRAFFIC INCREASE ACCESS TO THE COMMUNITY. EAST SAN FERNANDO VALLEY WILL THEN HAVE A PLANNED 6.7MILES OF 11 STATIONS 11 TRACTION POWER SUBSTATIONS OVERHEAD CONTACT SYSTEM 34 VEHICLES AND A MAINTENANCE AND STORAGE FACILITY.; INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: POPULACE OF LACMTA TRANSIT SERVICE AREA AND LOCAL AREA COMMUTERS; SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: LACMTA DOES NOT INTEND TO USE SUBRECIPIENTS.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
